artifacts.what: THE REFERENCE GRADIENT. Dropout in eval and at rate 0, num_recycles 0, trained weights, float64, per-parameter, None preserved. Validated against float64 central finite differences at 1.168e-03 worst over 16 stratified entries. Produced by run C; run D reproduced it bit-identically (evidence/det_selfdrawn/reproduction_A13.json).

the draws the reference gradient REPLAYED: recycle count, diffusion noise levels, all 45 torch.randn draws, both random.random values. Replay reported 0 mismatches. Match these or the comparison is void.
per parameter, whether it had a gradient at all. 0 absent of 4147, 4138 non-zero. None must match None; never fill with zeros.
the frozen batch, 5nw3, 56 tokens, already collated by their openfold_batch_collator. Fetch it; do not rebuild it.
the float64 weights the gradient was taken at, from of3-p2-155k.pt. Identical across runs C, D and E, so it is independent of which draws a run used. Needed for the trajectory, not for instrument A.
run C's own record, including every finite-difference check.
A13's detector: runs C and D compared per tensor. 4147 of 4147 bit-identical, worst 0.0, median 0.0, 0 over the 0.05 bar.

the same comparison WITHOUT CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8: 9 bit-identical, 55 over bar, worst 1.985, median 2.63e-14. This is what not pinning the deterministic kernels costs, and it lands on the near-zero-gradient tensors where a reader would misread it as model disagreement.

checkpoint.missing_note: The two layer_norm_z weights stay at their random initialisation. They are named here rather than buried: a consumer loading the same checkpoint into our stack must end up with the same two tensors unset, or the two sides do not start from the same w_0.
checkpoint.note: w0 is not shipped separately; it is this checkpoint, publicly downloadable.

consumer_rules: Use grads_f64_r0.pt, sha256 89457d8977327699c84fc90741a013bc369f835dea6008676492c786fb87f113, for instrument A. Check the digest before you read a byte: three gradients have been published here and the other two are in the `superseded` block with the reason each is dead.

Match draws_recycles0.pt before comparing anything. Run E is on the same host, r = 0, dropout off and named rebuild, and it differs from the reference only in having drawn its own randn values -- that alone moves the loss by 3.5e-02 and the global norm by 0.597.
Pin num_recycles to 0 on our side too. The recycle count changes what the gradient MEANS, not just how much work it is.
The recycle draw comes from OpenFold3.synced_generator, a private np.random.default_rng held as a model attribute (model.py:77). torch.manual_seed does not reach it.
None is not zero. Compare the presence pattern as a set before any magnitude. 0 of 4147 are absent here, 4138 are non-zero.
The gradient is BEFORE clipping. At world size 1 with accumulate_grad_batches 1 the optimizer-facing gradient is exactly grad * clip_coef, and clip_coef is 1.0 on this step.
Load of3-p2-155k.pt, not a random init. At a random init 2271 of 4890 weight tensors are exactly zero and the gradient reaches 6 of 4147 -- a comparison there is zero against zero.
Fetch the bytes and check the sha256; do not regenerate. Rebuilding on a different machine from the same seed gives 0/20 byte-identical batches while the entry order and token counts match.
Pin CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 and torch.use_deterministic_algorithms if you reproduce this. Without it two runs of the same graph disagree at worst 1.985 relative L2 on 55 tensors.

Do not compare this r = 0 gradient against the withdrawn r = 0.25 one and read the difference as a regression. They are two draws of DIFFERENT functions; the 2.256 / 1.971 / 1.563 worst relative L2 between them is the same order as the dropout floor itself.

determinism_floor.method: two processes, same seed, same batch, same box, float64
determinism_floor.note: file sha256 differs between two runs that agree to 1.9e-16, so a file-hash comparison is the wrong instrument; the hashes here verify a transfer, not a computation

finite_difference_validation.method: float64 central differences on the same forward, h = 1e-5, RNG pinned per evaluation
finite_difference_validation.sampling_rule: entries with |analytic| >= 1e-6, because 99.9 % of individual entries are exactly zero on a padded 56-token batch

pre_registered_targets.source: of3t-gradients, banked at commit 1d38c168c before this artifact existed, captured on qb2 CPU in float64 replaying the same draws at r = 0 with trained weights
pre_registered_targets.verdict: the count lands exactly; the two numbers do not, at 6.8e-03 and 5.4e-03 relative. That is materially larger than float64 rounding, so by pass 49's pre-decided rule an input is still uncontrolled. The draws were the dominant one and are now controlled -- before replay the same rebuild read loss 1.60736306238088 and norm 4.305010199537414, so replay closed 63 % of the loss gap and 97 % of the norm gap. What remains differs between an A100 float64 run and a qb2 CPU float64 run of the same graph on the same draws; the next suspects are the featurisation path the batch was carried in by hash to avoid, and how each side disables dropout. Open, and handed to of3t-gradients, who owns the other side.

what_changed: Dropout in eval AND at rate 0, so the artifact is an r = 0 reference: the mask is drawn from the device's default generator and an RNG-state snapshot reproduces a state, not a value, so a train-mode tape publishes one draw.

Deterministic kernels pinned (torch.use_deterministic_algorithms, CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8). Without the pin the eval-mode gradient still did not reproduce: 55 of 4147 tensors over the 5.0e-02 bar, worst 1.985, every one a layer_norm_z.bias whose gradient is a sum that cancels.

The draws are REPLAYED from draws_recycles0.pt rather than sampled. Putting Dropout in eval removes 61 consumers of the CUDA generator, which moves the diffusion noise (23.705, 5.853, 10.730, ... -> 2.612, 1.467, 5.936, ...). PROTOCOL 4a makes the draws inputs to the update rule, so the published run consumes the ones every consumer holds.

status: PUBLISHED. The reference gradient is grads_f64_r0.pt, sha256 89457d8977327699c84fc90741a013bc369f835dea6008676492c786fb87f113: trained weights, dropout in eval and at rate 0, num_recycles 0, float64, 4138 of 4147 tensors non-zero and 0 absent, agreeing with float64 central finite differences to a median 2.27e-04 and a worst 1.17e-03 over 16 stratified entries. Reproduced bit-identically by a second process, 4147 of 4147, worst 0.0. Two earlier gradients are withdrawn (train-mode dropout) and a third, run E, is superseded (self-drawn rather than replayed draws); all three digests are listed under `superseded` so a consumer holding an old one can tell which it has.

grads_f64_r0_rebuild.pt.kept_because: it is the measured cost of NOT replaying the draws: 4.305 against 3.708 on the same weights, same batch, same recycle count.
grads_f64_r0_rebuild.pt.why: SUPERSEDED, and this one is easy to consume by accident because its name says rebuild and it is r = 0 with dropout correctly off. It is the SELF-DRAWN run: its manifest reads replayed_draws null, so it drew its own 45 randn values instead of replaying draws_recycles0.pt. Its loss is 1.60736306238088 and its global norm 4.305010199537414, against the reference's 1.6422035029890711 and 3.707776369277739. It also carries no finite-difference validation, n_samples 0. It was shipped to qb2 in good faith by of3t-orchestrator's pass-62 transfer, which picked out_E off the box; the reference is run C, out_C.

grads_f64_recycles0.pt.why: WITHDRAWN. Taped in train mode, so the rate-0.25 Pairformer Dropout was live and the gradient was one draw. of3t-gradients measured its draw-to-draw floor at worst 1.167-2.419, median 0.48-0.55, an order of magnitude above the 0.05 bar it was being used at.

grads_f64_recycles3.pt.why: WITHDRAWN for the same reason, and never FD-validatable anyway at 3 recycles.

superseded.read_this_first: Three gradients have been published under this bundle and two are dead. Only grads_f64_r0.pt sha256 89457d8977327699c84fc90741a013bc369f835dea6008676492c786fb87f113 is the reference. Any other digest you were handed is one of these.

fd_at_h_1e-5.interpretation: truncation, not a wrong gradient: O(h^2 L''') on a curved trained surface, with samples now deep in the trunk. h-sweep 1e-3..1e-7 running.
fd_at_h_1e-5.resolution: h-independent disagreement on TRUNK parameters only, while diffusion-module entries converge to 1.785e-08. Cause: their trunk runs 4 recycling passes over the same weights and tapes only the last (model.py:230), so finite differences measure the TOTAL derivative through all four cycles while the analytic gradient is the PARTIAL derivative through the final cycle. Finite differences cannot validate a recycled trunk gradient by construction; re-run the validation at num_recycles = 0.

validated_gradient.bar: PROTOCOL 3d's per-tensor bar is 5.0e-02. The reference validates against finite differences at 2.18e-03 worst, 23x inside it, so the reference contributes nothing material to a measured disagreement.
validated_gradient.why_zero: Their trunk runs num_recycles + 1 passes over the same weights and tapes only the last (model.py:230). A finite difference perturbs the weight in every cycle and measures the TOTAL derivative; the analytic gradient is the PARTIAL derivative through the final cycle. At 0 recycles the two functions coincide, which is the only regime in which the trunk gradient can be validated at all. Evidence: hsweep.json.

what_it_is: One frozen training batch, the weights it was taken at, the per-parameter float64 step-1 gradient with its presence pattern, and every random draw the step made. This is the artifact PROTOCOL instrument A is measured against.
